attempted_claim: Let d>=5, a>-(d-2)^2/4, L_a=-Delta+a|x|^{-2} (Friedrichs), p>1+4/(d-2) so s_c=d/2-2/(p-1)>1. Let u be a radial maximal-lifespan focusing solution of (i d_t - L_a)u = -|u|^{p-1}u in dot H^{s_c}_a with sup_{t in I} ||u(t)||_{dot H^{s_c}_a(R^d)} < infinity. Prove I=R and u scatters in dot H^{s_c}_a as t-> +/-infinity; equivalently finite-time endpoint implies critical-norm blowup.
decisive_failure: Both the proof direction (missing focusing energy-supercritical rigidity lemma for the inverse-square operator under a bare uniform critical bound) and the disproof direction (no in-regime bounded-critical-norm blowup construction spanning d>=5 below the Joseph-Lundgren threshold) remain open; the retained script verifies only known identities and the cited papers supply the negative triage facts, so no part of the universal conditional-scattering claim is established here.
